messages:
matt: Heads-up — I landed the runtime metrics PR that adds per-model kv_cache_miss_rate and request_latency_p50/p95. Draft dashboard is at /dashboards/runtime/kv-cache. Need to sync alerting + pager routing before we flip it on for prod.
sarah: Nice. Can you paste the exact metric names? I want to wire them into the alert templates.
matt: Sure — metric names are `runtime.kv_cache_miss_rate{model,region}` and `runtime.request_latency_ms{quantile,model}`. The miss_rate is a gauge 0..1, reported every 10s. request_latency_ms is a histogram exported as quantiles.
diego: For alerts, I'd prefer to base paging on SLO burn rather than raw miss rate. Miss rate spikes happen during restarts but don't always affect customers.
jen: +1. What SLO are we targeting here? Is this for generation latency SLO or availability SLO?
matt: This dashboard maps to two SLOs: 99th perc latency for interactive (SLO: p99 < 1200ms) and request success rate (SLO: 99.9% success). Kv cache miss impacts both but we should use a burn-rate composite alert.
lena: Proposed thresholds: start with warn at 3% miss_rate sustained 5m (non-paging), page on miss_rate > 6% sustained 3m OR SLO burn > 5% in 10m. Thoughts?
sarah: That seems reasonable. For routing, infra incidents (OOMs, node disk) should go to eng-sre; anything that looks model-specific or routing fallback should go to eng-runtime oncall. Can we annotate alerts with `responsibility=infra|runtime` labels so pagerflow can route?
diego: We already have pager routing that picks teams by alert.labels.component, so yes — let's add label `component=runtime` or `component=infrastructure` when generating the alert.
jen: Small API debate: should the metric label be `model` or `model_variant`? Metrics folks prefer `model` (short) but ops wants variant for canary filtering.
matt: I added both: `model` (family) and optional `variant` (v1,v2-canary). The dashboard groups by `variant` by default and falls back to `model`.
lena: Runbook ask: please include a short triage checklist in the alert message. Example: 1) check recent deploys (link), 2) check runtime node CPU/GPU, 3) run kv cache health query. We can include quicklinks in the alert body.
sarah: Also add a non-paging slack notification to #runtime-alerts for the warn-level so product can eyeball before we page.
ops-bot: deploy detected: matt/core-runtime v1.9.4 -> prod in us-west (CI #3487)
matt: Good catch — if this coincides with a spike, that might be a deploy-induced regression. We should correlate with deploy tags.
diego: About the alert logic — suggest composite alert: (SLO_burn_rate > 5% for 10m) OR (kv_cache_miss_rate > 6% for 3m AND sustained increase vs 30m baseline). That reduces false positives.
jen: Agree. Also we should avoid paging during known maintenance windows. Is there a way to auto-suppress pages when `maintenance=true` label exists for a cluster?
sarah: Pagerflow supports runbook-suppression via silence windows. We can add an API to mark a cluster as under maintenance — but for now, add a `no_page` tag to alerts evaluated during scheduled window.
lena: Ops question: who owns the pager escalation? If runtime oncall doesn't ack in 10m, escalate to eng-platform to help with routing config.
sarah: That's our current policy. I'll add that to the alert policy: first page runtime-oncall, after 10m escalate to eng-platform, after 30m escalate to eng-sre.
matt: I'll draft the Prometheus alert rules — rough YAML below. Please review:
```
- alert: RuntimeKVCacheHighMiss
  expr: avg_over_time(runtime_kv_cache_miss_rate[3m]) > 0.06
  labels:
    severity: page
    component: runtime
  annotations:
    summary: "High KV cache miss for {{ $labels.model }}"
    runbook: "https://runbooks.company/internal/kv-cache"
- alert: RuntimeSloBurnHigh
  expr: increase(runtime_slo_burn_total[10m]) / 10m > 0.05
  labels:
    severity: page
    component: runtime
  annotations:
    summary: "SLO burn high for {{ $labels.slo }}"
```
jen: Need to replace `runtime_slo_burn_total` with our canonical metric name — is that `slo.burn_seconds` or `runtime.slo_burn`?
matt: Good catch — it's `platform.slo_burn_rate{service=runtime}` per the telemetry contract. I'll update.
ops-bot: alert created: silences applied for maintenance window us-west-2024-06-10T22:00Z -> 23:00Z
diego: One last ask — pin a canary dashboard that only shows variant=v2-canary and a lower alert threshold (to catch regressions earlier) but mark it non-paging.
sarah: Love that. We should add a rollout flag in the dashboard header so PMs can toggle canary vs prod view.
lena: I'll open the pager policy PR to add component-based routing and the escalation steps. Assigning to @sarah for review.
sarah: I'll review today. Can everyone add links to the dashboard panels they care about in the PR description? That makes triage much faster.
matt: Will do — PR: https://git.internal/reviews/6421 (runtime metrics + dashboard + alert rules). Please comment.
jen: Adding to oncall checklist: query to see if `variant` traffic < 1% before folding canary alerts into prod.
matt: Thanks all. Plan: land PR, wait 24h for metrics to populate, then enable warn-level notifications, watch for noise for 48h before enabling paging. If anyone sees repeated false positives, flag it here and we'll iterate.
sarah: Sounds good. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder: oncall rotation for eng-runtime starts in 2 days (pager schedule)
